correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=2, incidence identifies the flow subspace with the zero-row/zero-column matrices. The full S_m times S_n commutant has four distinct input-output cell-pair orbits, spanned by orthogonal component projectors; averaging any projection onto either invariant range produces the unique commuting P_Z or P_B without increasing its norm under any invariant ambient norm. Exact absolute column sums establish both endpoint minima and the integer equality boundary. For m=n=2, duality and equality in the triangle inequality force the unique dual projector functional. In every other size, a 2-by-2 alternating flow times a disjoint row/column summation functional yields nonzero perturbations preserving P_Z^2=P_Z; sign calculus shows all altered column sums unchanged for |t|<1/(mn), so a continuum of minimizers exists. The ell_p tensor identity follows from coordinate operator upper bounds and extremizing rank-one matrices. The actual embedded exact-rational checker verified 64 graph parameter pairs and 1936 columns; those finite cases are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete two-parameter optimization of natural cycle and cut subspaces over all linear projections, not merely evaluation of orthogonal projector norms. The sharp factorized formula extends to all entrywise ell_p norms and actually holds for any ambient norm invariant under independent row/column permutations, which provides a reusable structural criterion. The relative optimum norm crossing occurs exactly at (m-2)(n-2)=2, and the nontrivial qualitative rigidity dichotomy identifies exactly one biclique for which the ell_1 cycle projection minimizer is unique; every other case has explicit positive-dimensional optimizer freedom. These distinguish projection geometry beyond known pointwise norms. The work does not assert that its basic averaging method or the endpoint numbers alone are new.
